reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: BMI 51 sleeve gastrectomy with a known difficult mask and airway, semaglutide 3 days ago with vomiting yesterday, empagliflozin not held with an anion gap and ketonuria, undisclosed phentermine, and an SSRI meeting the surgeon's methylene blue leak test.

asa.rationale: BMI over 40 with severe OSA, T2DM, HTN, and mild pulmonary hypertension.

decision.rationale: Empagliflozin taken yesterday (should be held at least 3 days) with liquid diet, anion gap 18, CO2 18, and 2+ urine ketones is concerning for early euglycemic DKA; check beta hydroxybutyrate and a gas. GLP-1 effect with active nausea, vomiting, and prior retained food makes this a full stomach, and phentermine was taken yesterday. Reschedule with correct medication holds.

redFlags.finding: SGLT2 inhibitor not held, possible euglycemic DKA
redFlags.evidence: Empagliflozin last 10/26 0800; liquid diet 2 weeks; AG 18, CO2 18, urine ketones 2+, glucose 142 to 156; beta hydroxybutyrate not ordered.
redFlags.implication: Euglycemic DKA can be missed because glucose is near normal.
redFlags.action: Check beta hydroxybutyrate and ABG; postpone; hold empagliflozin at least 3 days before elective surgery.

redFlags.finding: GLP-1 agonist with symptoms of delayed gastric emptying
redFlags.evidence: Semaglutide 2 mg last 10/24; nausea, belching, full feeling today, vomited yesterday; EGD 09/2026 retained food after 12 h fast.
redFlags.action: Treat as full stomach (RSI, consider gastric ultrasound) or postpone; follow current multisociety GLP-1 guidance.

redFlags.finding: Documented difficult mask ventilation and difficult laryngoscopy
redFlags.evidence: 2019: grade 3 mask, VL grade IIb with bougie, SpO2 84%; MP IV, neck 50 cm, short TMD, beard; obstruction under propofol sedation twice.
redFlags.action: Ramped position, HFNO preoxygenation, VL first with bougie, awake intubation as an option, supraglottic and front of neck backup.

redFlags.finding: Serotonin syndrome risk with methylene blue leak test
redFlags.evidence: Sertraline 100 mg daily and tramadol PRN; surgeon plans methylene blue leak test.
redFlags.implication: Methylene blue is an MAO inhibitor; with SSRIs it can cause serotonin syndrome.
redFlags.action: Discuss an alternative leak test with the surgeon; avoid adding tramadol, meperidine, or other serotonergic drugs.

redFlags.finding: Phentermine taken yesterday, not in the bariatric record
redFlags.evidence: Pharmacy note 10/27: phentermine 37.5 mg daily, last 10/26 0700.
redFlags.implication: Sympathomimetic: hypertension and tachycardia, unpredictable response to indirect pressors like ephedrine.
redFlags.action: Ideally hold several days before surgery; if proceeding, use direct acting pressors.

redFlags.finding: Severe OSA, poor CPAP adherence, possible obesity hypoventilation, mild pulmonary hypertension
redFlags.evidence: AHI 48, CPAP use 41%, CPAP not brought; ABG PaCO2 47, HCO3 27, PaO2 68; RVSP 42.
redFlags.implication: Opioid sensitivity, postoperative hypoventilation, worsened pulmonary pressures with hypoxia and hypercarbia.
redFlags.action: Opioid sparing, awake semi upright extubation to CPAP, family to bring the device, continuous oximetry.

redFlags.evidence: Clindamycin ordered for penicillin anaphylaxis; weight 166 kg.
redFlags.implication: Current allergy guidance allows cefazolin in most penicillin allergic patients (dissimilar side chain); weight based dosing needed.
redFlags.action: Discuss cefazolin 3 g; if clindamycin is used, follow protocol coverage.

redFlags.finding: Anesthesia consent unsigned; difficult IV access
redFlags.evidence: Consents tab; two attempts for a 20 G.
redFlags.implication: Second access for a 2 h case in steep reverse Trendelenburg.

planItems.item: RSI or gastric ultrasound guided plan; ramped HFNO preoxygenation
VL first with bougie, difficult airway cart
Dose induction agents on lean body weight and NMB on ideal body weight
Pass the 40 Fr bougie carefully with OGT removed; communicate tube positions
Opioid sparing multimodal analgesia, surgeon TAP blocks
Full reversal, awake semi upright extubation to CPAP

boothComplications.why: Daily vaping with a reactive airway after intubation
Severe penicillin allergy history and antibiotic exposure
